CFI is looking for an international trainer for the project Media Lab Guinea Ecuatorial, funded by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.

The Service Provider would be responsible for designing and delivering training activities for journalists from Equatoguinean media outlets, in Malabo and Bata: a launch seminar for editorial managers, a training on the fundamental principles of journalism, content production workshops, and individual remote mentoring.
The project aims to strengthen the capacities of media outlets, journalists and content producers in Equatorial Guinea, and to develop young people's media and information literacy skills.

items.content_html:
CFI is looking for a media organization based in Jordan to design, produce, and disseminate an awareness-raising campaign addressing digital violence against people with disabilities engaged in political life, as part of the European Union-funded project Support to Democratic Reforms in Jordan.

The campaign aims to raise awareness among civil society actors, media professionals, and the wider public about the forms, consequences, and impact of digital violence on the participation of people with disabilities in political life. Through the production and dissemination of videos and podcasts, the selected organization will contribute to promoting a more inclusive, accessible, and participatory democratic environment.

The selected service provider will be responsible for producing and editing the audiovisual content, disseminating it through relevant media and digital platforms, and implementing communication and outreach activities to maximize audience reach and engagement. The provider will work in close coordination with CFI and the project's consultant throughout the production process.

Application deadline:
9 August 2026 at 1:00 PM (GMT+01:00 Paris, Brussels, Copenhagen, Madrid).

Please refer to the attached Call for Quotations for detailed information on the scope of services and application requirements.

As part of the European Union-funded AGILE project, CFI is seeking service providers to design and deliver three 4-day community journalism training sessions across Central Asia and Uganda. 
Each four-day session will bring together approximately 15 participants from marginalised communities, covering foundational journalism skills, storytelling, mobile journalism, and podcast production. 
Three lots are available: one in Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan) and two in Uganda. 
Applicants may apply for one or two lots.

Place of performance: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Uganda.

Application deadline: 1st June 2026 at 04:00 p.m. CET

As part of the Empowering Palestinian and Israeli Civil Societies and Media project, funded by the European Union and implemented jointly with Expertise France, which aims to strengthen the role of independent media and civil society, promote reliable and fact-based information, and counter disinformation, CFI – the French Media Development Agency – is launching a call for projects to provide content production stipends to freelance journalists and content creators to support the development of high-quality content across digital media and social platforms. 

These stipends will enable journalists and content creators in both Palestine and Israel to produce diverse, engaging, and credible content that reaches a broad audience and promotes accurate, balanced narratives.

Objective

Provide financial support to content production editorial projects for a period of up to 6 months between May and October 2026 for up to 40 independent journalists and content creators.

Submission on CFI platform
